doc.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005

title: JoAnn Chmielowski on how she met Al and began accompanying him
summary: JoAnn explains meeting Al sixteen years ago and promoting him online.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: I’m pleased to be joined by JoAnn Chmielowski. And I got a little bit of insight about how this working relationship started, but I’d like to hear it again if you don’t mind.

Oh sure. This is above everything a symbiotic relationship because Al is the long term memory of his career and I’m kind of the short term memory. But really what I am is a kind of fan gone berserk. I met Al I guess — oh now my daughter is 17 — I met Al 16 years ago. He was playing in a restaurant that I was at. And I couldn’t believe what I was hearing. And I said how could this be, in Oneonta, that there is such a musical quality like this. Because I’d been living here maybe about ten years, originally from the New York City area, Brooklyn. I worked in Manhattan and you know, so I was used to when you go see something it’s like top notch. And I moved up here and things were quite good entertainment wise, but not like this. So I started talking to Al and he spoke the same dialect as my grandparents. And I said oh, I found a paisan. And we struck up a relationship like that. And I was working at the restaurant at the time. And one night the keyboard was unoccupied and I sat in. And jokingly he said to me, “Oh keep practicing, I’ll hire you in a few years.” And I didn’t really think he was serious but you know with that thought in mind I just kept practicing. And I probably kept practicing for about six or seven years when he needed a keyboard player, piano player, for a wedding that was in a cornfield, literally in the middle of nowhere. The Scarpino wedding, right? We still have it on tape. So he figured well the people were from Virginia, the other side of the family were from Brooklyn, the cornfield was out in the middle of nowhere, and he said well this is a good time to take chance on this person because when she blows it it won’t matter. So we were out there and we played and after that we were hooked. And I found that what I did was have this mission that had, oh my gosh, people have to know about this man. And it was just in the beginning of the Internet. And I had just gotten a computer. And I think without that tool it would have been really difficult for me to really promote Al and his things, and to do the writing that needed to be done for publicity without the word processor, because well I had a job, I had a young family, my children were little, so it because like kind of my mission.
It’s definitely the ways in which we can promote ourselves and others these days has changed rapidly and I’m glad that Al is here to take advantage of that and that you can help him in doing that.
Yeah because he said he didn’t even have a radio. And now we have the Internet.
Yeah. And now you’re all over the Internet.

I can’t believe how this all came about. She is the one. She put me on the map. And of course I helped put her on the map too. But she is really, really — where would I be if I had not met her? I’d be doing a few gigs here and there. Now I’m known all over the world.
